Event Recap · Show & Tell: AI for GTM

Watch AI run real go-to-market workflows

Such a packed room and great energy at the Show & Tell: AI for GTM event. I walked away with a ton of new ideas — including clever ways to connect tools you're probably already using, like Notion · Clay · Slack · Salesforce, to get up-to-date information in a clearer, more streamlined way.

If you're curious about what AI inside real workflows looks like, these demos are worth your time. I saved the highlights (and a few live clips) below.

The demos, in detail

Each with a concrete takeaway, the real tools behind it, and a clip where I caught one on video.

Notion

Customer Hubs

Eric Goldman

  • Bringing all of your customer data into one central place — instead of it living scattered across a dozen tools and team handoffs.
  • Pulls together Salesforce, Gong, Zendesk, meeting notes, internal tasks and requests, and more, so every team is working from the same context.
  • The payoff: less time hunting for information across systems, more time acting on a complete picture of the customer.

Upside

GTM Engineer Hub + Live Job Board

Mada Seghete

  • A live database of ~1,491 job listings (806 open), 2,015 named practitioners, and 1,142 hiring companies — sorted into eight archetypes of the role, from Outbound GTME to Executive / Center-of-Excellence Lead.
  • The GTM Engineer job board is a live mirror of Notion, rebuilt daily: bots discover roles (Exa API, ATS, LinkedIn), enrich and dedupe them, and re-publish the site on every deploy.
  • A "Relationship Radar" app turns an attendee list into a curated who-to-meet plan — matching target accounts, customers, and prospects to the people in the room.

Baseten

Monitoring GTM Signals with Parallel

Ben Levitt

  • A "Monitor" is a saved web search that runs on a schedule and reports new signals or events matching a spec — think LinkedIn, company websites, and press releases, defined with a natural-language prompt, an output schema, and a frequency.
  • Baseten runs tens of thousands of monitors daily to prioritize accounts, personalize outbound, catch new accounts that aren't yet in the CRM, and keep TAM / startup territories fresh.
  • Every detection comes back as a structured, evidence-backed event (with citations and a confidence level), and reps push up/down feedback via Slack to keep tuning the monitors.
What Baseten tracks per account
  • Funding, M&A, and capital events
  • AI product and feature launches
  • AI/ML engineering & product leadership hires
  • AI/ML engineering & product leadership job posts
  • AI technical content — engineering blog posts, research, talks, and case studies that show how AI features are being built

Browserbase

How to Win Agent-led Growth

Jay Sahnan

  • Browserbase makes the web programmable as APIs so agents can reliably extract data and act on any site — 10,000+ companies are building on it.
  • Agent-led growth is already moving numbers: in three months they doubled the customer base, grew self-serve revenue 119%, and lifted activation by >10%.
  • A growing share of new signups now say they "heard about us from AI" — a channel worth designing for, not just watching.

Assembled

Re-engaging Closed-Lost Deals

Maitrik Shah, Growth Marketing Manager

  • The goal: reopen dialogue with deals you lost in the past — closed-lost is warm history, not a dead end.
  • Make sense of unstructured deal history and turn it into context, then auto-draft emails and LinkedIn messages and create cold-call tasks.
  • Spin up a custom, personalized web page per prospect with the info most likely to re-engage them.
Rules of building
  • When building for multiple teams, use tools everyone can manage — in their case, that's Clay.
  • Everything should be a function in Clay, and each function should tell you what to do next — like skills in Claude or components in Figma.
  • Minimize the number of inputs — they use only an Account ID for internal data and a Website for external data.

Samsara

Skills Hub & "stop-slop"

David Benac

  • A shareable "skill" that teaches Claude (or any LLM) to catch and remove the tells of AI writing — filler phrases, throat-clearing openers, emphasis crutches, and formulaic structures. Outbound that doesn't read like AI slop.
  • Skills Hub is the catalog: install a skill with a one-liner, share your own, and see install stats — GTM craft, packaged and distributed like code.

This isn't just a GTM thing

While this was a GTM-focused session, the same principles translate directly to day-to-day operations — building out dashboards, monitoring client or data signals, or tracking workflow updates.

Instead of spending time aggregating data, your team gets that time back to focus on the insights and the impactful follow-up.

Signals over static lists · agents as a real channel · GTM craft shipped like software.
